title: KDE and GNOME Developers Ponder How to Handle AI-Generated Contributions
content:
KDE and GNOME Developers Ponder How to Handle AI-Generated Contributions (gnome.org) 40
			
		 	
				Last weekend KDE's annual Akademy conference included a presentation proposing
an AI-native KDE," writes The Register.  This led KDE developer Nate Graham to open a discussion about proposed restrictions on LLM-assisted contributions which "rapidly became heated. Moderators issued warnings, restricted further comments, and eventually removed the thread."
 
But as Graham writes on his blog, "A bunch of people mostly outside of KDE who disapprove of LLM usage derailed KDE's attempt to add restrictions to LLM usage." Two people unknown to any KDE contributors appeared and began fighting with one another about the broader topic of the morality of AI, not the proposed guidelines... Someone else outside of KDE set up kdeforpeople.com in an attempt to... pressure KDE into banning LLMs. A bunch of people signed onto it, almost none of whom are known KDE contributors. The topic was picked up on social media and the press with... varying levels of accuracy. The draft proposal was removed and the whole topic hidden... Yep, that's where we're at in the state of online discourse around AI...
 
The "lovable, sovereign, AI-native KDE" idea was presented by two people important to KDE in decades past, but who had not made any contributions recently besides this Akademy talk. Their idea does not reflect the overall direction of KDE or Plasma, and I don't think it ever will. If "a lovable, sovereign, AI-native KDE" freaks you out, I believe it is completely reasonable and safe to ignore...
 
I completely understand why a lot of people have problems with LLMs. I have these concerns as well.
He concluded by asking people not to derail any future process to set usage guidelines, fighting over "the broader topic of AI in general."
 
"The discussion is gone, but the argument continues," adds The Register: GNOME developer Jordan Petridis has also published The GNOME LLM Policy That I Want, proposing that LLMs be barred from creating or modifying anything submitted to GNOME or hosted on its infrastructure.
"You might be asked to prove your code meets this requirement," Petridis writes, arguing for proposals that target the norms around developer behavior. His rationale? "The GNOME Project prioritizes the social and human aspects of collective software creation,"

report.summary: KDE 与 GNOME 就如何对待 AI 生成代码贡献陷入政策争论
report.background: 随着 LLM 编程助手普及，开源社区开始面对一个现实问题：AI 生成的补丁、翻译、文档是否可被接受，如何标注、由谁担责。KDE 在年度 Akademy 大会上出现"AI 原生 KDE"的演讲，随后开发者 Nate Graham 发起关于限制 LLM 辅助贡献的讨论，却因大量非 KDE 社区外部人士涌入争论 AI 伦理而失控，草案被撤回。与此同时，GNOME 开发者 Jordan Petridis 也提出了自己的 LLM 政策建议，主张全面禁止 LLM 生成内容进入 GNOME 的代码与基础设施。
key_points: KDE 内部原本想给 LLM 辅助贡献立规矩，讨论帖却因外部人士吵架、刷签名网站施压而被迫删除隐藏。
"AI 原生 KDE"只是两位多年未参与贡献的老成员在大会上的个人演讲，并不代表 KDE 与 Plasma 的官方方向。
发起讨论的 KDE 开发者 Nate Graham 本人也认同对 LLM 的担忧，但呼吁别把具体规则讨论变成泛化的 AI 道德大战。
GNOME 开发者 Jordan Petridis 提出更激进的方案：禁止 LLM 创建或修改任何提交到 GNOME 及托管在其次的代码，甚至可能要求贡献者自证。
两件事共同暴露了开源社区在"人味"协作文化与 AI 提效工具之间的深层张力，目前尚无统一共识。
report.impact: 对 AI 行业而言，这是继版权、训练数据争议后开源治理层面的新战线，AI 编程工具的"合规可用边界"将被社区规则重新定义；对开发者来说，未来提交 PR 可能需附带 AI 使用声明甚至人工改写证明，工具链会被迫内置溯源与披露功能；对普通用户，短期内桌面环境与开源软件的质量和更新节奏可能受贡献流程变严的影响，但社区强调的人类主导、可问责原则有助于维持软件信任度。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注 GNOME 的 GitLab 政策讨论、KDE 的 discuss.kde.org 与 Akademy 演讲回放；实践层面可参考 GitHub Copilot、Cursor、Aider 等工具的 AI 使用声明配置，以及 Linux 内核、Fedora 等已出台的 AI 贡献披露指引，学习如何用 Developer Certificate of Origin 加 AI 标注模板规范提交。
